results.title: Mirae Asset says faster credit growth versus slower deposit growth tightens Indonesian bank liquidity
results.body: The article reports that national bank credit grew 13.3% year‑on‑year in August 2026 while deposits (DPK) rose only 7.7% year‑on‑year, indicating tightening liquidity. Total credit reached IDR 9,019 trillion and DPK IDR 9,733 trillion, with the CASA ratio at 64.6% and headline LDR at 92.7%, which would rise to about 97.2% after removing SAL liquidity of IDR 451 trillion. Mirae Asset Sekuritas remains selective, maintaining a positive outlook on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) but cautioning larger state‑owned banks as tighter funding may pressure margins and asset quality. On 25 September 2026 the stocks of PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) rose modestly, while PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) fell, reflecting market reaction to the liquidity environment.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) posts higher profit but net interest margin drops below 6%
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) reported a net profit of Rp 34.77 trillion for the first eight months of 2026, up 6.63% year‑on‑year, while its net interest margin fell to 5.94% (5.32% in August), slipping below the 6% threshold for the first time. Credit disbursements grew 13.66% year‑on‑year to Rp 1,446.98 trillion, interest income rose 0.22% to Rp 109.66 trillion, interest expense fell 6.70% to Rp 32.41 trillion, yielding net interest income of Rp 77.25 trillion (up 3.44% yoy), leaving the margin well under the FY26 target range of 7.4‑7.8%.

results.title: Foreign investors' net selling makes ten stocks, including PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI), top losers as the IHSG falls
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp559 billion on Friday, 25 September 2026, making ten stocks the largest foreign outflow victims while the IHSG weakened by 56.7 points (0.9%) to 6,241.8 at market close. Net sell in the regular market amounted to Rp440.3 billion and Rp118.7 billion in the negotiation and cash markets, with total transaction value reaching Rp9.3 trillion. The biggest foreign sell-offs were PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with Rp62.8 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) with Rp37.8 billion, PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) with Rp29.2 billion, TLKM with Rp112.7 billion and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk with Rp71 billion. Overall, 122 stocks rose, 587 fell and 254 remained unchanged during the session.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold Rp 4.39 trillion this week, with banks leading the top‑selling stocks
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 4.39 trillion across the market during the week ending 26/9/2026, contributing to the IHSG’s 3.09% decline to 6,241.89 points. The ten most net‑sold stocks were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Rp 1.1 trillion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Rp 676.34 billion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Rp 597.42 billion, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Rp 478.55 billion, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) Rp 213.79 billion, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) Rp 159.15 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) Rp 125.58 billion, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) Rp 96.45 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) Rp 74.93 billion and PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) Rp 72.91 billion.

results.title: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.16 trillion in PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) over the past month
results.body: Foreign investors net sold Rp1.16 trillion of PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) between 25 August and 24 September 2026. During the same period they also posted net sells in PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) while net buying Rp480.43 billion of PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI). On 24 September 2026 foreign investors sold about Rp1.49 trillion overall and the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed down 1.20% at 6,298.61. Bank Indonesia kept the BI‑Rate at 5.75% with the Deposit Facility at 4.75% and the Lending Facility at 6.50%.

results.title: IHSG falls to 6,298.61 as foreign investors net sell Rp1.49 trillion across ten stocks, led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI).
results.body: On Thursday 24 September 2026, the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,298.61, down 1.20%, as foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.49 trillion, comprising Rp1.42 trillion in the regular market and Rp71.85 billion in the negotiation and cash market. The largest outflows were in PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with Rp141.17 billion and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) with Rp74.90 billion, placing them among the ten most heavily sold stocks that pressured the market.

results.title: Indonesia Stock Index (IHSG) Potentially Exposed to Rising U.S. Treasury Yields
results.body: The article discusses the potential impact of rising U.S. Treasury yields on the Indonesia Stock Exchange Composite Index (IHSG). On 24 September, IHSG fell 1.2% to 6,298.61 amid foreign investors' net sell of Rp 1.49 trillion and higher oil prices. Foreign selling targeted shares of big banks BMRI and BBRI and telecom firm TLKM, contributing to the index's weakness. Analysts forecast further testing of support around 6,186-6,200 (or 6,254/6,146) and resistance near 6,400, with the index's direction tied to continued U.S. Treasury yield increases.

results.title: Foreign investors ramp up net selling, surpassing Rp 100 trillion
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors' net selling on the Indonesia Stock Exchange has exceeded Rp 100 trillion year‑to‑date, reaching Rp 104.3 trillion in the regular market. The biggest outflow was on PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) with a net sell of Rp 531.9 billion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) at Rp 141.1 billion, while PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) recorded the largest net buy of Rp 24.4 billion. On Thursday 24 September 2026 the composite index (IHSG) closed down 76.3 points (‑1.2%) at 6,298.6, with total market turnover of Rp 11.2 trillion, as higher U.S. Treasury yields (10‑year >5%, 2‑year ≈4.9%) and a stronger dollar pressured Indonesian assets.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold a record Rp 1.49 trillion as the IHSG fell, with PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) topping the list of heavily shorted stocks.
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 1.49 trillion across the Indonesian market on 24 September 2026, contributing to a 1.20 % decline in the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) to 6,298.60 points. The market saw 462 stocks close lower, total trading volume reach 29.03 billion shares worth Rp 10.82 trillion, and all sector indices weaken, the raw materials sector falling 2.17 % as the most corrected. The ten most heavily shorted stocks were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) with a net sell of Rp 531.94 billion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Rp 133.24 billion, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Rp 84.61 billion, PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) Rp 51.65 billion, PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA) Rp 39.70 billion, PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) Rp 32.60 billion, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) Rp 32.03 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) Rp 24.71 billion, PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) Rp 24.02 billion, and PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY) Rp 17.52 billion.

results.title: UOB Kay Hian recommends buy on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) and hold on PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) amid tighter funding conditions
results.body: UOB Kay Hian’s research notes that Indonesian banks are tightening funding strategies as liquidity remains constrained, and the broker maintains a buy rating on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) while assigning hold to PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI). BBCA’s credit portfolio expanded 10.5% year‑on‑year to August 2026 with CASA growth of 10.8% YoY and a loan‑to‑deposit ratio of 81%, while BMRI’s credit grew 17.6% YoY, CASA rose 8.2% YoY and LDR reached 94.4% (potentially 101% excluding government SAL funds). BMRI relies heavily on non‑DPK funding, holding Rp 341 trillion in repo, interbank loans and securities (about 21% of its credit), compared with BBCA’s Rp 28 trillion (3% of credit), and Tier 1 capital ratios fell to 20.4% for BBRI (down 199 bps), 16.4% for BMRI (down 180 bps) and 15.5% for BBNI (down 270 bps) in the first half of 2026. The analyst notes that dividend payout ratios may be trimmed for BBRI and kept around 65% for BBNI in 2026, and that the banking sector remains cheap but UOB Kay Hian will monitor funding strength and capital adequacy before adjusting its stance.

results.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends buy for major Indonesian banks amid retail credit pressure
results.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (BRIDS) maintains buy recommendations for PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (target price Rp 8,600), PT Bank BTPN Syariah Tbk (BTPS) (Rp 1,400), PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk (BNGA) (Rp 2,100), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp 6,200), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) (Rp 4,800), PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) (Rp 3,100), PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk (BBTN) (Rp 1,500) and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) (not rated). The sector trades at roughly 1.5× price-to-book, about two standard deviations below its five-year average, while national credit expanded 13.65% yoy in August 2026, with investment credit growing 25.11% yoy, consumer credit growing 5.07% yoy, and consumer-related NPLs rising to 2.4-2.5% (KPR 3.3%, apartment 4.3%, vehicle 2.6%).

results.title: IHSG falls 1.20% to 6,298.61; analysts see support test at 6,200‑6,254 on Friday
results.body: The Indonesia Stock Exchange Composite Index (IHSG) closed down 1.20% at 6,298.61 on Thursday amid foreign‑investor selling of about Rp 987 billion, higher oil prices and rising US Treasury yields. Analysts highlighted support levels at 6,254 and 6,146 and resistance at 6,352 and 6,429, while also noting a potential test of the 6,186‑6,200 range with support at 6,200 and resistance at 6,400 on Friday. The index traded below its 5‑day and 100‑day moving averages, with MACD in negative territory and Stochastic RSI in oversold condition. The sell‑off targeted major bank stocks BMRI, BBRI and telecommunications firm TLKM, which were among the shares hit by foreign investors.

results.title: Technical stock recommendations for PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), and PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (HRTA) for Friday (25/9).
results.body: The article issues technical trading recommendations for PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (HRTA) ahead of Friday, 25 September 2026. AADI closed at Rp 11,150 on Thursday, down 1.11% daily, with a speculative‑buy target supported at Rp 10,550 and resistance at Rp 11,750; BBRI closed at Rp 3,140, down 1.57%, with a buy entry suggested above Rp 3,150‑3,160, support at Rp 3,050 and resistance at Rp 3,320; HRTA closed at Rp 2,310, up 0.43%, trading above its MA10 of Rp 2,219 and with a buy‑on‑break recommendation at Rp 2,350, support at Rp 2,190 and resistance at Rp 2,500. The recommendations were provided by senior analysts Nafan Aji Gusta of Mirae Asset Sekuritas, Achmad Yaki of BCA Sekuritas and Oktavianus Audi of Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia. The broader market context showed the IHSG index ending at 6,298, down 1.20% with a total transaction value of Rp 11 trillion across 26.5 billion shares.

results.title: Seven Indonesian banks report the highest net profits for the first half of 2026.
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) posted a net profit of Rp31.18 trillion, up 17.5% YoY; PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) earned Rp30.41 trillion, up 24.4% YoY; PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) recorded Rp29.54 trillion, up 1.8% YoY; PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk posted Rp10.80 trillion, up 6.33% YoY; Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) reported Rp4.15 trillion, up 11.08% YoY; CIMB Niaga posted Rp3.43 trillion, down 2.2% YoY; and OCBC Indonesia posted Rp2.73 trillion, up 6.39% YoY. Credit disbursements expanded across the banks, with BRI reaching Rp1,580.42 trillion (UMKM 75.1% of the portfolio), Mandiri expanding to Rp1,592 trillion, BCA’s CASA reaching Rp1,082 trillion (84.3% of DPK) and credit of Rp1,036 trillion, BNI’s credit rising to Rp968.53 trillion, and CIMB Niaga’s credit growing 12.13% to Rp193.19 trillion, while BNI’s NPL stood at 1.9% and Mandiri’s at 0.98%. The strong earnings occurred in a macro environment of 5.3% GDP growth and 3.34% inflation. CIMB Niaga’s profit decline reflected pressure on interest margins despite a 25% rise in non‑interest income and an 87.22% jump in other income, whereas OCBC Indonesia’s results were supported by integration with the OCBC Group and growth in intermediation and cheap funding.

results.title: Bank Indonesia Holds BI Rate at 5.75% and Panin Sekuritas Lists PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) as Top Buy Picks.
results.body: On 23 September 2026 the Rapat Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia kept the BI Rate at 5.75% with the deposit facility at 4.75% and the lending facility at 6.5%. The spread between the BI Rate and the U.S. Fed rate narrowed to 1.75% from 2% and August bank credit growth rose 13.65% year‑on‑year, supporting a positive outlook for interest‑rate‑sensitive stocks. Panin Sekuritas highlighted PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) as its top buy recommendations, assigning 12‑month target prices of Rp3,856, Rp8,157, Rp5,221 and Rp4,384 respectively. Analyst consensus shows strong buying interest, with 23 analysts recommending BBRI, 35 for BBCA, 29 for BMRI and 24 for BBNI, reflecting expectations of continued credit expansion and a stable rupiah.

results.title: Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BBRI) announces limited review and upcoming publication of its Q3‑2026 financial statements
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) disclosed that its consolidated financial statements for the period ending 30 September 2026 will undergo a limited review by a public accountant and will be published in accordance with applicable regulations. In the first half of 2026, BRI and its subsidiaries reported a net profit of Rp30.86 trillion, up 17.42 % YoY, driven by a 5.42 % increase in interest income to Rp107.92 trillion and a 5.87 % decline in interest expense to Rp27.39 trillion, yielding net interest income of Rp80.53 trillion (+9.91 %) while impairment provisions rose 9.64 % to Rp25.51 trillion. Profitability ratios improved, with pre‑tax ROA at 3.30 %, after‑tax ROA at 2.70 % and ROE at 22.59 %, although the net interest margin fell to 6.40 % from 6.58 %, reflecting broader banking‑sector margin pressures.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) lead foreign net sell list as IHSG rebounds.
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rebounded on Wednesday, closing at 6,374.91, up 97.86 points (1.56%). Despite the market gain, foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp461.35 billion across the market, with 448 stocks advancing, 186 declining and 159 unchanged. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net sell were PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) (Rp187.64 bn), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp128.73 bn), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) (Rp124.67 bn), PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) (Rp66.49 bn), PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) (Rp45.77 bn), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) (Rp35.30 bn), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) (Rp31.01 bn), PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) (Rp28.87 bn), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) (Rp28.27 bn), and PT AKR Corporindo Tbk (AKRA) (Rp20.33 bn). Total trading volume reached 36.09 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp12.54 trillion.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) shares see net foreign sell offset by domestic buying, closing up 0,31%
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) shares recorded a net foreign sell of Rp 187.64 miliar on 23/9/2026, while domestic investors posted a net buy of Rp 187.6 miliar. Based on data from Stockbit Sekuritas, domestic investors net bought Rp 187.6 miliar, with Stokcbit Sekuritas (Rp 30.5 miliar), CGS International Sekuritas (Rp 26.7 miliar) and BCA Sekuritas (Rp 23.8 miliar) contributing, helping the stock close up 0.31% at Rp 3,190. For semester I‑2026 the bank reported PATMI of Rp 31.2 triliun, a 17.5% yoy increase, with net interest income up 9.9%, pre‑provision operating profit up 12.8%, cost of credit improving to 3.1%, total credit rising 16.2% yoy to Rp 1,645.5 triliun (corporate credit +47.1%, commercial credit +58.1%) and the micro‑credit portfolio at Rp 714.1 triliun, while gross NPL fell to 2.90% and loan at risk (LAR) improved to 9.1%. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia maintains a buy recommendation with a 12‑month target price of Rp 4,000, implying a P/BV of 1.8 kali versus a three‑year average of 2.06 kali, while flagging risks from prolonged NIM pressure, tighter liquidity, slower credit growth, higher cost of credit and delayed micro‑asset quality recovery.

results.title: Foreign Investors Pull Back, Leading Stocks See Heavy Selling
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 461.3 billion across the Indonesian market on Wednesday, 23 September 2026, while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose 97.87 points (1.56%) to 6,374.9 at the close. The largest foreign outflows were in PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with a net sell of Rp 187.6 billion, followed by BMRI with Rp 128.7 billion, TLKM with Rp 124.6 billion, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) with Rp 35.3 billion. In total, foreign investors sold Rp 468.2 billion in the regular market, while net buying in the negotiation and cash market amounted to Rp 6.9 billion. Overall market turnover reached Rp 12.8 trillion, with 464 stocks rising, 200 falling and 299 unchanged.

results.title: Foreign Net Sell Surpasses Rp 100 Trillion, Keeping PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Under Pressure
results.body: Foreign investors' net selling in the regular market reached Rp 102.9 trillion year‑to‑date, topping the Rp 100 trillion threshold and pressuring key stocks. On Wednesday, total foreign net sell across the market was Rp 460.7 billion, with the largest outflows in PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) at Rp 187.6 billion, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) at Rp 128.7 billion and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) at Rp 124.6 billion. Conversely, PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) attracted a net foreign buy of Rp 106.7 billion and PT Timah Tbk (TINS) a net buy of Rp 53.7 billion, while the Indonesia Stock Exchange Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 97.8 points (1.5%) at 6,374.9 with total transaction value of Rp 12.8 trillion. Market commentator Hendra Wardana said the modest index gain reflected a positive reaction to Bank Indonesia’s decision to keep the BI Rate at 5.75% despite the continued foreign outflows.
